name: Depth and Geometry Supervision
text:
# Depth and Geometry Supervision

Also called: Geometric Regularization, Depth Priors

## Overview
Depth and Geometry Supervision methods enhance [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF)](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md) optimization by incorporating explicit geometric constraints—such as depth maps, 3D points, or structural priors—into the training loss. While [standard NeRF](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) relies solely on photometric consistency, which can lead to shape-radiance ambiguity and degenerate solutions (e.g., "floaters") in sparse-view settings, these methods enforce geometric plausibility [S1, 8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. They differ from sibling methods like [Diffusion-regularized NeRF](7381-diffusion-regularized-nerf.md) by using deterministic geometric signals rather than generative priors, and from [Volumetric Supervision](11100-volumetric-supervision.md) by focusing on surface-level or depth-distribution alignment rather than volumetric density regularization [S1, 8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate within an augmented loss structure where the [total loss](#4177-total-loss-function.md) $\mathcal{L}_{\text{total}}$ is a weighted sum of the standard [photometric reconstruction loss](#7799-photometric-reconstruction-loss.md) and one or more [regularization terms](#1413-regularization-losses.md) $\mathcal{L}_k$ [S1, 7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md, 8582-regnerf.md]:

$$ \mathcal{L}_{\text{total}} = \mathcal{L}_{\text{photo}} + \sum_k \lambda_k \mathcal{L}_k $$

where $\lambda_k$ are hyperparameters controlling the strength of each regularizer [S1, 7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md, 8582-regnerf.md]. The [photometric loss](#9563-photometric-loss-rawnerf-variant.md) is typically the [Mean Squared Error](#1651-mse-loss-and-psnr-conversion.md) (MSE) between the rendered color $\mathbf{C}$ and the ground truth image $I$:

$$ \mathcal{L}_{\text{photo}} = || \mathbf{C} - I ||_2^2 $$

Regularization terms $\mathcal{L}_k$ operate on the density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$ fields, the rendered weights $w_i$, or the final rendered images to constrain the solution space [S1, 7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md, 8582-regnerf.md]. The gradients of these terms are backpropagated through the [differentiable volume rendering](#43-differentiable-volume-rendering.md) process to update the [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) parameters [S1, 8582-regnerf.md]. Common strategies include enforcing spatial smoothness, ensuring geometric consistency across views, aligning the output distribution with learned priors, or matching semantic embeddings.

## Subtopics

### [Geometric Baseline Regularization](7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md)
[Geometric Baseline Regularization](#7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md) prevents degenerate solutions in few-view settings by combining photometric loss with three geometric priors: foreground absorption, frustum consistency, and depth distribution compactness. It differs from [Depth-Supervised NeRF](8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md) by relying on internal consistency rather than external depth maps, and from [Depth Structural Consistency Regularization](9371-depth-structural-consistency-regularization.md) by using explicit frustum intersection counts.

### [Guided Optimization of NeRF](7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md)
This method mitigates shape-radiance ambiguity by restricting sampling ranges along camera rays using adapted monocular depth priors. It computes adaptive bounds based on cross-view geometric consistency errors, concentrating samples around plausible depths, and refines output depth using confidence scores.

### [Single-view NeRF Training with Depth Map](8679-single-view-nerf-training-with-depth-map.md)
This method addresses single-view reconstruction by initializing geometry using a 360-degree depth estimation prior. It explicitly fuses multiple perspective depth estimates into a canonical panorama depth map via deformable alignment before integrating it into the [NeRF training loop](#970-nerf-training-loop.md), rather than relying on implicit regularization.

### [Depth-Supervised NeRF](8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md)
DS-NeRF incorporates sparse 3D depth priors from Structure-from-Motion (SfM) to accelerate convergence and improve quality with fewer views. It enforces that the rendered ray termination distribution aligns with surface locations estimated by SfM, using KL divergence to match the distribution to a Gaussian model of keypoint uncertainty.

### [Depth Structural Consistency Regularization](9371-depth-structural-consistency-regularization.md)
[RDSC](#9371-depth-structural-consistency-regularization.md) enforces geometric continuity by aligning the structural relationships of rendered depth pixels with a prior depth map (e.g., DepthAnythingV2). It constrains relative depth differences between neighboring pixels to match the prior, preserving sharp edges while smoothing noise, rather than enforcing direct pixel-wise matching.

### [Statistical Depth Refinement](10185-statistical-depth-refinement.md)
This technique mitigates overfitting to noisy depth priors by replacing outlier depth values with smoother estimates from an underfitting model state. It identifies corrupt pixels based on residual statistics (quantile threshold) and patches them with the underfitting depth, differing from standard supervision by actively filtering noise rather than applying uniform loss.

### [Novel View Regularization](10806-novel-view-regularization.md)
This approach mitigates shape-radiance ambiguity by injecting synthetic rays into the [training loop](#4290-training-loop.md) to provide additional geometric supervision. It actively samples unobserved directions to guide optimization toward geometrically plausible solutions, preventing overfitting to sparse viewpoints.

### [3D Point Supervision Loss](12693-3d-point-supervision-loss.md)
This term minimizes the distance between 3D points backprojected from rendered depth and ground-truth 3D points. It enables robust pose registration in sparse-view regimes by enforcing a global geometric connection between training images and scene geometry, unlike DS-NeRF which struggles with local ambiguities.

#### Coarse-Fine Consistency Loss
- **Definition**: A loss function that enforces consistency between depth estimates of the [coarse and fine NeRF](#3406-coarse-to-fine-nerf.md) models to prevent ineffective hierarchical sampling and blur [S1].
- **Formula**: $L_{cfc} = \mathbb{1}_{\{m_f=1\}} \odot ||z_c - \hat{\nabla}(z_f)||^2 + \mathbb{1}_{\{m_c=1\}} \odot ||\hat{\nabla}(z_c) - z_f||^2$, where $z_c$ and $z_f$ are coarse and fine depths, and $m_c/m_f$ are reliability masks determined by reprojection [S1].

#### Zero-level set projection
- **Definition**: Refines inaccurate median depth from a pre-trained NeRF, particularly at grazing view angles, by iteratively projecting points onto the zero level-set of the surface using TSDF values [S2].
- **Step**: For each 3D point $p$ on the viewing ray, perform exactly 4 iterative gradient descent steps along the ray direction using the TSDF predicted value to update the point position [S2].
- **Formula**: $p_{new} = p_{old} + \alpha \times \hat{t}$, where $[\hat{t}, \hat{n}, \hat{f}] = \phi(p)$; $p$ is the current 3D point, $\alpha$ is a small constant step size, $[\hat{t}, \hat{n}, \hat{f}]$ are the tangent, normal, and feature outputs from network $\phi$ evaluated at $p$ [S2].
- **Parameter**: $\alpha$: Small constant controlling the step size of the gradient descent update. Value not specified in this section [S2].
- **Pitfall**: Median depth from a pre-trained NeRF becomes inaccurate when the angle between the view direction and the surface is small (grazing angles) [S2].
- **Usage**: Applied in NeRFMeshing as a preprocessing step to initialize the mesh geometry before training the SSAN model [S2].

#### Robust Depth Loss
- **Definition**: A loss function designed to address geometry error degradation in extrapolation performance by being less sensitive to outliers than [L2 loss](#6038-mean-square-error-mse.md), encouraging NeRF to terminate rays around pseudo depth while retaining freedom for inaccurate geometry [S3].
- **Formula**: $\mathcal{L}_{\text{robust}}(\mathbf{r}) = \begin{cases} 0.5\Delta D(\mathbf{r})^{2}, &\text{if } \Delta D(\mathbf{r}) < \beta \\ \beta^{2} (0.5 + \log (\frac{\Delta D(\mathbf{r})}{\beta})), &\text{otherwise } \end{cases}$ where $\Delta D(\mathbf{r}) = \hat{D}(\mathbf{r}) - D(\mathbf{r})$ is the absolute depth difference, $\beta$ is a constant set to 0.1, and $\hat{D}(\mathbf{r})$ is the depth expectation along the camera axis of ray $r(t)$ [S3].
- **Parameter**: $\beta$: A constant threshold for the robust depth loss, set to 0.1 throughout the experiments [S3].

#### Depth Supervision with Planar Architectural Depth Priors
- **Definition**: Incorporates precomputed depth estimates for floor, ceiling, and walls into NeRF training to enforce geometric constraints on textureless planar surfaces [S4].
- **Step**: 1. Compute depth estimates for floor, ceiling, and walls using semantic segmentation. 2. Incorporate these priors into training with MSE and BoundL losses alongside photometric loss. 3. Train until convergence [S4].
- **Parameter**: $\delta$ (BoundL tolerance): 1 mm. $\lambda_{color}$: 10 (bedroom), 1 (living room). $\lambda_{depth}$: 10 (bedroom), 1 (living room) [S4].
- **Number**: [RMSE](#10453-depth-accuracy-metrics.md) of priors vs ground truth: 2.786 mm (bedroom), 3.201 mm (living room). Converged in 120,000 iterations [S4].
- **Comparison**: Faster convergence than photometric-only (120k vs 200k) and patch-regularization (120k vs 280k) methods due to depth supervision enabling quick identification of empty spaces, concentrating sampling on occupied regions, and providing a stronger optimization signal [S4].

#### Indirect Depth Supervision (KL Loss)
- **Definition**: A [regularization technique](#11314-regularization-techniques.md) that uses depth priors to constrain the NeRF weights by aligning the probability distribution of rendering weights with the depth prior, specifically using KL divergence [S5].
- **Formula**: $L_{KL} = \sum_{i}^{N_r} \sum_{t=t_n}^{t_f} D(r_i) - \epsilon \log w_k \exp(-\frac{(t - D(r_i))^2}{2\hat{\sigma}^2}) \Delta t_k$, where $w_k$ are rendering weights, $t_k$ are sampled points, $\Delta t_k$ are distances, $D(r_i)$ is ground truth depth, $\epsilon$ is a kernel parameter, and $\hat{\sigma}$ is a variance parameter [S5].
- **Parameter**: $\epsilon(x)$: A kernel that integrates to one (a distribution) with a bounded domain parameterized by $\epsilon$ [S5].
- **Pitfall**: The URF loss (Urban-NeRF) has no open-source implementation, so KL loss is selected as the representative for indirect supervision [S5].

#### Geometry and Opacity Regularization
- **Formula**: [Sparsity loss](#1203-nerf-training-configuration.md): $L_S = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} O(i)$, where $N$ is number of rays intersecting the 3D box, encouraging sparse opacity to suppress floaters. Opacity loss: $L_O = -\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} [O(i) \cdot \log(O(i)) + (1 - O(i)) \cdot \log(1 - O(i))]$, encouraging opacity values to be 0 or 1 to avoid translucent effects [S6].

#### Depth Filtering with RGB Confidence
- **Definition**: Filters predicted depth maps by computing a per-pixel confidence metric based on the reconstruction error between predicted and ground truth RGB images [S7, unofficial].
- **Step**: Load predicted RGBs and depths from NeRF results directory. Load ground truth RGBs from the data directory. Compute confidence map by taking 1 minus the mean absolute error between normalized predicted and ground truth RGBs across channels. Pass ground truth RGB, predicted depth, confidence map, and save path to a parallel processing pool for filtering [S7, unofficial].
- **Parameter**: worker_num: Number of parallel workers for the multiprocessing pool, default 8 [S7, unofficial].

#### Direct Depth Supervision
- **Definition**: A [training objective](#8586-regularization-and-loss-functions.md) that directly compares the depth rendered by the NeRF with a ground truth depth prior using a pixel-wise loss function [S5].
- **Step**: First sample a batch of $N_r$ rays, then compare the rendered depth and ground truth depth with different loss functions (MSE or L1) [S5].

#### GeoAug
- **Definition**: An approach that uses data augmentation by rendering new training images with new noisy camera poses using DSNeRF as a baseline and using [depth as regularization](#7616-depth-regularization.md) [S8].

## Background
The concept of integrating geometric priors into NeRF training emerged to address the "shape-radiance ambiguity" and the tendency of NeRFs to overfit to photometric signals, resulting in artifacts like "floaters" and incorrect geometry, especially in sparse-view scenarios [S1, 8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. Early work, such as DS-NeRF, demonstrated that sparse 3D points from Structure-from-Motion (SfM) could serve as effective, "free" supervision signals to guide the density field [S1, 8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. Subsequent research expanded this to include monocular depth priors [S1, 7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md], structural consistency from dense depth estimators [S1, 9371-depth-structural-consistency-regularization.md], and robust losses to handle noisy stereo data [S3]. The field has evolved from simple L1/L2 depth matching to more sophisticated distributions (KL divergence) [S1, 8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md], hierarchical consistency [S1], and 3D point-based registration [S1, 12693-3d-point-supervision-loss.md]. These methods are widely used in applications requiring high geometric fidelity from limited data, such as indoor reconstruction [S4], sparse-view synthesis [S1, 12693-3d-point-supervision-loss.md], and mesh extraction [S2].
